To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists (IL-1ra), acting in the cytosol of intestinal epithelial cells, inhibit IL-1-induced cytokine production through inhibition of p-38 mitogen- activated protein kinase and NFkappaB pathways.
icIL- 1Ra1 inhibited cytokine-induced IL6 and IL8 production through the inhibition of p38MAPK and NF-kappa pathways in Caco- 2 intestinal epithelial cell line.

icIL- 1Ra1, a novel intracellular IL-1 receptor agonist (IL-1ra) splice variant, inhibits IL-8 and IL-6 production in Caco2 intestinal epithelial cell line through p38 MAPK and NF-kappa B signaling pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists in the regulation of cytokine production by intestinal epithelial cells.
the role of IL-1 in intestinal epithelial cells, and the mechanisms of action of IL-1 and its naturally occurring inhibitor (IL-1 receptor antagonist).
the role of intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists in the pathogenesis and treatment of inflammatory diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intracellular IL-1 receptor type 1 inhibitory protein (icIL- 1RI) is a novel anti-inflammatory cytokine that acts intracellularly to inhibit IL-1 signaling in intestinal epithelial cells by inhibiting p38 MAP kinase activity and NF-kappa B activation, and thus inhibits IL-6 and Il-8 production.
icIL- 1Ra1, a novel intracellular IL-1 inhibitor, inhibits IL- 1-induced IL-8 production via the NF-kappaB and p38 MAP kinase pathways.
the intracellular IL-1 receptor type 1 antagonist, icIL-RA1, inhibits IL-6 and 8 production in C2 cells via p38 MAP kinase pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists (IL-1RAs) may play an important role in regulating IL-1-mediated inflammation and that intracellular IL-RAs may be useful as a novel therapeutic strategy in the management of inflammatory bowel diseases.
the icIL-1ra1 protein is a potent inhibitor of the inflammatory response in the intestinal epithelium, acting through the inhibition of the p38 MAP kinase pathway.
intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists are a new mechanism for regulation of inflammatory response in intestinal epithelial cells and other cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists may have important functions in regulating inflammatory responses.

the intracellular form of IL-1 receptor antagonists may play a role in the regulation of cytokine production in the intestinal epithelial cells and may be involved in the regulation of intestinal inflammation.
intracellular IL-1 receptor antagonists (icIL-RA), such as icIL-1RA1, may be important in regulating intestinal inflammation.
